title: Hail! Holy, Holy, Holy Lord
description: Hail! Holy, Holy, Holy Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 259.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail! ho-ly, ho-ly, ho-ly Lord! Whom One in Three we know; By all thy heav-enly host a-dored, By all thy church be-low.

lines: Whom One in Three we know;
By all thy heavenly host adored,
Thy universe is full of thee,
Thee, Spirit of truth and holiness,
Which angel-choirs, and saints in light,
And both the choirs ere long shall join,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
